title: more cons than pros
text:
more cons than pros. I've had this vacuum for 3 months, and got it off of QVC with more attachments than on here, but I never use the microfiber mop anyway. I'll put brackets around reviews for the attachments that don't apply to this amazon package but for someone who was wondering about the extra pieces (which you can see here on the QVC website [...]

This vacuum sucks a lot of stuff out of our carpet. With a dog and two cats we have a lot of pet hair around, and every time I'm done vacuuming the canister is full of dirt and hair.

The cord isn't a long or short length. I use a vacuum extension cord anyway, but if I don't then I need to change the outlet once or twice while vacuuming my main floor.

[I use the bare floor attachment for my kitchen. It works okay, but when you run it parallel to the wall, it won't get any dirt or crumbs against the baseboard. Instead, you have run it at a perpendicular angle, so that's a little annoying since I have to often run over the same floor twice in two different directions just to make sure I get all the dirt/crumbs around the edges, and it forces you to slowly make your way down the wall a foot at a time, only as wide as the nozzle. It's irksome to say the least. I think I'll just start sweeping before I vacuum, which is pretty annoying.]

[I haven't used the dry dust mop attachment (microfiber pad) because I haven't had any real use for it when I have the bare floor attachment. The kitchen is high-traffic area and for the amount of crumbs from food and dog food that land on the floor, I'd rather use the bare floor piece rather than the dust mop. If I had a wood floor without as much traffic I might use it, but the rest of my house is carpeted!]

The regular "motorized floor brush nozzle" works well. I have to cut out the hair from the spinning brushes every few uses--it's amazing how much of my own long hair ends up on the carpet (gross, I know). I don't think it gets the edges of my carpet very well either, but I didn't seriously expect it to.

I wish the turbo brush could have somehow been motorized, but it wasn't with my last vacuum either so I didn't really expect it to be. I use it on my carpeted stairs, and it works ok but could definitely work better and more efficiently if it was motorized.

The vacuum is very tippy, [especially with the bare floor attachment. It almost can't stand up on its own with that attachment], so I always lean it up against a wall anytime I need to stop vacuuming (that goes for both floor attachments I use, [but the bare floor one hardly stands up at all without tipping over).]

My biggest issue with this vacuum is the "stretch hose." On the vacuum itself, it is 22" long. When fully extended, it's as long as 65". They want you to detach the floor attachment and use just the handle with stretch hose (with other attachments), OR you can detach the extension wand and use it with a floor attachment (like the dust mop piece in the pictures on QVC, turning the vacuum into a canister vacuum rather than upright).

However, the resistance of the hose is so strong that you can't extend the hose without holding on to the vacuum itself or else the vacuum gets dragged along with you (or tips over at the very least). If I wanted to use the vacuum as a canister vacuum rather than an upright, it'd be nearly impossible to do so since you can't tow the canister along with you. I have the biggest problem while using it on the stairs. I wish I could leave it at the top or the bottom of the stairs and use the handle with the turbo brush, but I can't go more than one step without the vacuum falling over because the resistance is so strong on the hose once you stretch it in the slightest. Instead, I detach the canister from the floor piece and extension wand, and just try to hold it in one hand while using the nozzle handle in my other hand. It's a big pain that I wasn't prepared for with this vacuum.

Overall, I don't think I'd recommend this vacuum just because of the inconveniences I have with it. I'm not very excited that I know I'll be stuck with this vacuum for a least a few years before I can try something else. All of the attachments make you excited about it, but I don't think they make up for the cons. The high ratings really made me think it'd be fantastic, but unfortunately I just don't think it's all that it's worked up to be.

11/7/2012 Edited to Add: I forgot to mention that this thing is a pain to empty. The bin holds very little until it is at is "max full." But if you have any sort of pet hair then it gets all clumped up in the top of the bin instead of the bottom. The bin is shaped so that all the hair/dust/dirt gets caught way up inside it and you have to reach your fingers up to pull it all out. I can't imagine this being possible for anyone with bigger fingers than I have, and my hands are fairly small. Another reason I'm very disappointed with this vacuum. Cannister vacuums are supposed to be easy to empty--just tip the bin upside-down and everything pours out. This vacuum is the opposite of that scenario.

product_metadata.title: Shark NV352 Navigator Lift Away Upright Vacuum, Hepa Filter, Anti-Allergen Technology, Swivel Steering, Ideal for Carpet, Stairs, & Bare Floors, with Wide Upholstery & Crevice Tools, Lavender
features: LIFT-AWAY FUNCTIONALITY: lift away the detachable pod and easily clean above-floor areas like stairs, furniture, and more.
ANTI-ALLERGEN COMPLETE SEAL TECHNOLOGY: Works with a HEPA filter to trap dust and allergens inside the vacuum cleaner.
POWERFUL & LIGHTWEIGHT : Powerful suction to deep-clean carpets and tackle bare floors with a lightweight design for effortless portability.
BRUSHROLL SHUTOFF: Feature allows you to instantly switch from deep carpet cleaning to gentle bare floor cleaning.
SWIVEL STEERING: Easily maneuver your vacuum in and out of tight spaces, in corners, around furniture, and more.
PERFECT FOR PETS: Powerful pet hair pickup attachments like the wide upholstery tool make cleaning pet hair a breeze.
CREVICE TOOL: Access corners, baseboards, tight spaces, and ceilings for versatile cleaning.
WHAT'S INCLUDED: Shark Navigator Upright Vacuum, Wide Upholstery Tool & 12" Crevice Tool.
description: A lightweight 2-in-1 Lift-Away upright vacuum with a detachable pod for portable cleaning power. With the push of a button, Lift Away the pod to easily clean in hard-to-reach areas. This vacuum is also equipped with Swivel Steering for excellent control when maneuvering around furniture, and has a completely sealed system with a HEPA filter to trap dust and allergens.
